cells.tense: You're at the far end of a long stretch, and what you built is in your hands.
cells.ask: Take the finished thing to one person today — hand it over, or start the first step of what it was for. Letting it meet what comes next shows you what it's good for.
cells.core:
On a normal day here you take what you know into what you don't, one step at a time, no map needed. Whatever you finished last stays close by, and you walk into the unclear parts with it, without making a ceremony of it.

What's different now is that the work itself is done. Not a draft, not a maybe — a real thing, and you're the one who brought it here. That weight is what an ending feels like when it's honest, and it's also what you get to set down and use. The next unknown is easier to walk into with something real in your hands.
cells.sheetLine: You carried it to the end, and it's yours to use now.
cells.verb: carrying what you started to its end
cells.place: moving on the light you have, without the whole road

cells.tense: You're already living past the ending, arranging a future that hasn't been written.
cells.ask: Name one thing you can see in front of you today — just describe what's there, out loud or on paper, without deciding what it means. Seeing clearly is what brings you back to the step you're actually on.
cells.core:
On an ordinary day here you look at what's in front of you, take the next step it shows you, and let the rest stay unknown. That's the whole method. You don't need the full road in order to move.

Right now you're trying to finish something that isn't finished, and the pushing makes everything harder to read than it needs to be. You want the ending settled before the middle is done. The step you're on is the only one you have, and reaching for ten more is what's draining the room. What's real is smaller than what you're bracing against.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing for an ending that hasn't been written.

cells.tense: Something ended behind you, and you're still standing where it happened.
cells.ask: Let one person tell you what they notice about where you are right now — not advice, just what they see. Hearing it from outside opens the feeling that's waiting, and that's the way back to the step in front of you.
cells.core:
There's a way this goes well here: you stay open enough to be moved by what's actually in front of you, and you let the next thing reach you before you know what it is. That kind of seeing doesn't close anything down. It keeps deepening, and it's how the unclear parts stay walkable.

Something real is behind you, and you've left the pen down. You're not in the room where the work is anymore. You're somewhere else, looking back at a closed door, and the looking keeps you from the only step that's available. What finished is finished; what's in front of you hasn't been met yet.
cells.sheetLine: You finished something and stopped moving with it.
cells.verb: carrying what you started to its end
cells.place: moving on the light you have, without the whole road

cells.tense: You're still writing the next page, but it's filed under someone else's hand.
cells.ask: Say 'I made this' about one piece of how things stand — the timing, the call, the thing you say anyone would have done. Claiming it is how you get back to the simpler truth of who did the work.
cells.core:
The way this looks when it's going well here: you take the next step while it's still taking shape, without waiting for the whole picture, because working without one is what you already do. That's what brought you to this point, and it runs quietly while you're busy with other things.

You're steering this. You choose what happens next, change the path where it needs it, decide — and the words you use make it sound as though the movement were just how things are going. The work of choosing is happening. Saying so isn't. The next step is yours to take, and it has been yours every time you took one.
cells.sheetLine: You're making this happen and calling it circumstance.
